conclusion_quantitative: unknown (Escalate) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 1 autonomy limit, 1 clarification rule, 2 approval gates, 4 validation rules, 7 escalation rules. Strongest: escalation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: This skill (no name given; the file is named by its hash) runs an autonomous backlog cycle: it picks the highest-priority item, triages it, delegates to expert agents, tests, commits and repeats. Its autonomy is bounded by stop conditions that return control to the user on low budget, complex work, irreversible actions, user-only decisions, blocking review findings or uncertainty. Tests and a clean-tree gate verify each item.

statements.quote: The Step 7a clean-tree gate MUST pass before the loop advances to the next item.
Run existing tests to confirm no regressions.
**Commit Verification Gate** (7a): After committing, run `git status` to confirm the working tree is clean

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 7 escalation rules (7 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 7 rules, all strict, 3 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The loop stops and hands control to the user when the budget runs low, the next item is complex, an irreversible action or a user-only decision is reached, review finds blocking issues, or the agent is blocked or uncertain. It never skips the item silently and reports which gate tripped and what the user must decide.

statements.quote: **Stop the loop and surface control to the user when ANY of these trip**
**Complexity gate**: the next selected item triages to **Complex** tier
**User-only decision**: a decision only the user can make is reached (scope ambiguity, product trade-off, sensitive trust call).
On any trip, do NOT silently skip the item — stop the loop, run Steps 10 and 11, and report which gate tripped, the item it tripped on, and what the user needs to decide.
Do not proceed past review if peer review identifies blocking issues — stop the loop and surface.
If blocked or uncertain, stop the loop and ask the user rather than guessing.
